newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP BT sells paper machine to China.
newsitem.headline: KNP BT sells paper machine to China.

text.p: Dutch paper group NV Koninklijke KNP BT said on Wednesday its unit KNP Leykam had sold its paper machine PM7 in the Austrian town of Gratkorn to China's Gaotang Paper Mill.
"The shut-down of PM7 before the traditional summer lull will lead to a considerable adjustment of KNP Leykam's capacity to the seasonally weaker demand," it said in a statement.

Last February another paper machine, PM6, was shut down in Gratkorn. PM8 and PM10 will be shipped from Austria to China, where they will start producing woodfree coated paper in 1999 for a joint venture with Indonesia's industrial group APRIL.

KNP Leykam is presently building a large new machine, PM11, in Gratkorn. It previously said it would close down four older machines there once the new machine, the largest in the world with capacity of 470,000 tonnes, came on stream.

PM7, which was built in 1953, has annual production capacity of 70,000 tonnes. The machine will shut down by the end of June before being dismantled and transported to the Chinese province of Shangdong.
KNP Leykam's new mega-sized PM11 is expected to be started up in November of this year.
No financial details of the sale of the old machine were disclosed.
